title: One Profile to Rule Them All
subtitle: A Case Study in Persistent Multi-Tier AI Companionship — Martin Grobbelaar, July 2026

sections.heading: The Paper
sections.content: Most AI assistants treat every session as a fresh start. This paper argues for an alternative: a single persistent identity that accumulates memory, skills, and taste over months of daily use. We compare three conditions across 15 controlled runs — a blank agent, a skill-configured agent, and a fully evolved profile — and find that the evolved profile produces consistently higher quality output, tighter variance, and spontaneously reproduces learned aesthetic preferences (Catppuccin dark mode, unprompted).

sections.heading: Key Findings
items: Consistency over capability: C3's output range was ±4 files vs C1's ±23 — a 5.75× improvement in reliability
Delegation is stochastic: C2 delegated ~50% of the time. Skills enabled but did not guarantee advanced patterns
Token efficiency improves with memory: C3 reduced token consumption 64% across runs (2.2M → 799K)
Learned aesthetic transfer: C3 spontaneously produced Catppuccin Mocha dark mode without being prompted — C1/C2 never did across 10 combined runs
Cost-effective: the entire N=5 benchmark cost less than a cup of coffee per condition

sections.heading: The Architecture
sections.content: Three tiers share one identity: an Orchestrator (routine work, relationship holder), a Worker (local Hermes 3 8B, cost-free, autonomous tasks), and an Analyst (deep reasoning, code audits). Specialists are intentionally stateless — they receive task briefs, execute, and return results. Only the Orchestrator knows who the user is.

sections.heading: The Quote That Says It All
sections.content: "The other agents know my name, but not who I am." — the user, comparing the evolved profile against a stateless interface running the same underlying model.
